literal: Prince of Pengcheng
idiomatic: The Prince of Pengcheng

literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie, style Yanhe.
idiomatic: Xie, Prince of Pengcheng, styled Yanhe.

literal: From youth precocious and sharp; his bearing and nature were not of the common sort.
idiomatic: From childhood he was precocious and sharp; in bearing and temperament he stood apart.

literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Shiping and made Palace Attendant and General Who Conquers the West.
idiomatic: In Taihe year 9 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shiping and made palace attendant and general who conquers the west.

literal: When Xie was born his mother Lady Pan died; that same year Xianwen passed away.
idiomatic: Xie was born the year his mother Lady Pan died; that same year Xianwen passed away.

literal: When he came to understanding he petitioned to observe mourning for her.
idiomatic: Once he could understand, he petitioned to mourn her properly.

literal: Empress Dowager Wenming would not permit it; he therefore wasted away three years and took no part in joyous celebrations.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming refused; he wasted away for three years and joined no festive occasion.

literal: Gaozu marvelled greatly at him.
idiomatic: Gaozu was deeply struck by him.

literal: Keen and addicted to study, never setting it aside day or night; broadly mastered classics and histories; elegantly fond of composing prose.
idiomatic: Quick-witted and devoted to books, he studied day and night without pause, mastered the classics and histories broadly, and loved to write.

literal: When Gaozu was founding the realm, he was relieved of Palace Attendant and general and appointed Grand Master for the Glorious.
idiomatic: While Gaozu was still founding the realm, Xie was relieved of palace attendant and general and made grand master for the glorious.

literal: Again made Palace Attendant, on long duty within the forbidden interior, deliberating great affairs of army and state; of the myriad reins nothing was not his to share.
idiomatic: He was again made palace attendant and kept long watch inside the palace, sharing in every great decision of army and state.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Xie was made Acting General Who Pacifies the Army, commanding the army of imperial clansmen, guarding close at night.
idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Xie was made acting general who pacifies the army, took command of the clansmen's guard, and slept in attendance at his side.

literal: When the five ranks were established, fief of two thousand households; transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Palace Attendant as before; enfeoffment changed to Prince of Pengcheng.
idiomatic: When the five ranks were instituted he received two thousand revenue households, became director of the secretariat while remaining palace attendant, and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng.

literal: Gaozu with attendant ministers ascended the Jinfeng city wall, looked back and saw behind the hall parasol trees and bamboo, and said: "The phoenix does not perch except on the parasol tree and does not eat except bamboo seeds; now parasol tree and bamboo both flourish—can a phoenix descend?
idiomatic: Gaozu climbed the Jinfeng wall with his attendants, glanced at the parasol trees and bamboo behind the hall, and said, "The phoenix perches only on the parasol tree and eats only bamboo seed. Both are lush now—will a phoenix come down?"

literal: " Xie replied: "The phoenix comes in response to virtue—how could parasol tree and bamboo bring it down?
idiomatic: Xie answered, "The phoenix answers virtue. How could trees and bamboo summon it?"

literal: " Gaozu said: "By what do you say so?
idiomatic: Gaozu asked, "On what grounds?"

literal: " Xie said: "In the time of Shun of Yu the phoenix came with ceremony;
idiomatic: Xie said, "Under Shun of Yu the phoenix came in ritual order;"

literal: when Zhou rose, the luan and zhuo birds cried on Mount Qi.
idiomatic: when Zhou rose, the luan and zhuo cried on Mount Qi.

literal: One has not heard of descending for parasol trees or eating bamboo.
idiomatic: No one ever heard of a phoenix coming down for timber or bamboo alone.

literal: " Gaozu laughed and said: "I too have not hoped for a descent.
idiomatic: Gaozu laughed. "I never expected one either."

literal: " Later he feasted the attendant ministers in the Clear Emblem Hall.
idiomatic: Later he feasted his attendants in the Clear Emblem Hall.

literal: The day grew late; they moved to beneath the fragrant grove at the Transforming Flow Pool.
idiomatic: As the day waned they moved to the fragrant grove by the Transforming Flow Pool.

literal: Gaozu said: "At the start of the earlier feast ruler and ministers were all solemn; toward the end the cups began to loosen and the flowing light was about to fall—yet we did not fully enjoy it, still lingering on the afterglow; therefore I have again summoned you.
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "At first we were all stiff with ceremony; near the end the wine began to flow freely, yet the light was failing before we had our fill. I still hunger for that glow, so I have called you back."

literal: " He then looked up at the parasol leaves' lushness and said: "'Its parasol, its chair-tree, fruit hanging thick; a gracious prince—none without fine deportment.' Now the worthies beneath this grove are enough to fill a song.
idiomatic: He looked up at the thick parasol leaves and quoted, "'Parasol and chair-tree, fruit hanging thick; gracious princes, none without fine bearing.' The men in this grove are fit for verse."

literal: " He then ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Guang to read the late-spring poems the ministers had composed on imperial command.
idiomatic: He ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Guang to read the late-spring poems composed on imperial command.

literal: When they came to Xie's poem Gaozu still altered one character for him and said: "In old times Qi Xi recommended his son and the realm called it utmost fairness; now seeing Xie's poem I know the Director of the Secretariat's recommendation was not private.
idiomatic: At Xie's poem Gaozu changed one character himself and said, "When Qi Xi recommended his own son the realm called it perfect fairness. Your poem shows my secretariat director did not favor you privately."

literal: " Xie replied: "Your subject exposed this clumsy work and thereby showed the holy court's favoritism; relying on the divine brush's correction I may have a fair reputation.
idiomatic: Xie replied, "By showing this clumsy verse I only exposed the court's partiality. Your brush's correction is what gives it any reputation at all."

literal: " Gaozu said: "Though one character is carved away, it is still the jade's own body.
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Even carved by a single character, it remains jade in substance."

literal: " Xie said: "Your subject has heard that in the three hundred poems one phrase can sum them up.
idiomatic: Xie said, "They say the three hundred poems may be summed in a single line."

literal: Now Your Majesty's gift of carving one character is enough to equal a linked city in price."
idiomatic: Your Majesty's one-character revision is worth a city of jade."

literal: Xie memorialized to resign as Palace Attendant; an edict said: "The beauty of the cicada-fur cap awaits you to shine; in a season when men are lacking, how can you step back?
idiomatic: Xie asked to resign as palace attendant. The edict read, "The court's dignity waits on you to shine. In a season when talent is scarce, how can you withdraw?"

literal: If you can think earnestly and become sage, there will surely be material for it.
idiomatic: "If you set your mind to it, you will have much to give."

literal: " Later, when Gaozu favored the northern capital, they halted at Tongdi Mountain in Shangdang.
idiomatic: Later, on a journey to the northern capital, the court halted at Tongdi Mountain in Shangdang.

literal: Beside the road were more than ten great pine trees.
idiomatic: More than ten great pines stood beside the road.

literal: At that time Gaozu advanced under an umbrella and went on composing a poem, sending someone to show Xie and say: "I have just begun this poem; though not in seven paces, it is not far off either.
idiomatic: Gaozu walked on under his umbrella composing a poem and sent word to Xie: "I have just started this piece. It may not be seven paces, but it is not far off."

literal: You may compose one; by the time you reach where I am, finish it there.
idiomatic: "Compose one yourself and finish it by the time you reach me."

literal: " At that time Xie was more than ten paces from the emperor; he therefore composed as he walked and finished before reaching him.
idiomatic: Xie was still ten paces behind; he wrote as he walked and finished before he arrived.

literal: The poem said: "I ask the pine grove—how many winters has the pine grove known?
idiomatic: His poem ran: "I ask the pine grove—how many winters has it seen?"

literal: How are mountains and rivers unlike the past? Wind and clouds are the same as of old.
idiomatic: "Are mountains and rivers unchanged? Wind and clouds are as they were of old."

literal: " Gaozu laughed greatly and said: "Your poem also tunes its blame at me.
idiomatic: Gaozu laughed aloud. "Your poem rebukes me as well."

literal: " An edict said: "Younger brother Xie's birth mother Lady Pan departed early in years; a splendid title was not yet added. Xie's grief was born with his body and pain rose with his form. Now, because he extends his thought, there is ample cause for pity; she may be posthumously enfeoffed Grand Consort of the Pengcheng state to comfort the living and the dead.
idiomatic: An edict said, "Younger brother Xie's mother Lady Pan died young without a posthumous title. His grief has been with him from birth. Moved by his devotion, posthumously enfeoff her as Grand Consort of Pengcheng to comfort living and dead alike."

literal: " Again he was made Director of the Secretariat, Palace Attendant as before.
idiomatic: He was again made director of the secretariat while remaining palace attendant.

literal: When Gaozu campaigned south against Hanyang he made Xie acting Grand General of the Center Army and added one set of martial music.
idiomatic: When Gaozu marched south against Hanyang he made Xie acting grand general of the center army and granted a set of martial music.

literal: Because favors came in quick succession Xie spoke to his face and said: "Your subject has heard that joining near and far in one post and establishing different and same together—this was already written in the past; your subject wishes to recite it for the future.
idiomatic: Favored again and again, Xie spoke plainly: "I have heard that to join near and far in one office and to set unlike with alike was written long ago. I wish to recite it for what comes after."

literal: Chen Si sought and was not granted; this foolish subject did not seek yet obtained.
idiomatic: "Chen Si asked and was refused; I did not ask and was given."

literal: How could it be only that past and present differ in saying so—the encounter of fortune and misfortune differs greatly; it is not only that Cao Zhi from afar envies your subject—it is also that Your Majesty treads where Emperor Wen of Wei would not look.
idiomatic: "Past and present are not the only divide—fortune and misfortune differ as well. It is not only that Cao Zhi envies me from afar; Your Majesty walks where Emperor Wen of Wei would not tread."

literal: " Gaozu laughed greatly, took Xie's hand and said: "The two Caos envied each other's talent and fame; I and you are kin by virtue. On this account I need not blush before the former exemplars.
idiomatic: Gaozu laughed and took his hand. "The two Caos were jealous of each other's gifts; you and I are joined by virtue. On that score I need not blush before the ancients."

literal: You need only restrain yourself and return to ritual—what more is needed?"
idiomatic: "Only restrain yourself and return to ritual. What more is there?"

literal: Gaozu personally lectured on mourning garments in the Clear Emblem Hall and said at ease to the assembled ministers: "Yanhe, Jiyu and the others are still in tender years; they early donned the cap and sash; they lost the training of the courtyard and have not yet learned ritual; I have often wished to have them understand mourning garments once from me.
idiomatic: Gaozu lectured on mourning dress in the Clear Emblem Hall and told the ministers at ease, "Yanhe, Jiyu, and the others are still young. They took cap and sash early, missed the courtyard's instruction, and do not yet know ritual. I have often wished to explain mourning dress to them myself."

literal: On examining myself my understanding is thin and floating; I therefore suppressed it and did not permit it.
idiomatic: "Reviewing my own understanding, I found it shallow and held back."

literal: Recently, because I was sitting drunk, I suddenly assented; therefore I have bent the court's worthies and now personally transmit the explanation.
idiomatic: "Lately, drunk in my seat, I assented without thinking, and so I have bent the court's worthies to hear me teach it now."

literal: As I am about to take the lecturing seat I am ashamed and my feelings tremble.
idiomatic: "As I take the teacher's seat I am ashamed and my heart trembles."

literal: " Imperial Censor Zhongwei Li Biao replied: "From antiquity until now there has never been a Son of Heaven who lectured on ritual.
idiomatic: Imperial censor Li Biao answered, "From antiquity until now no Son of Heaven has lectured on ritual."

literal: Your Majesty's sagacity and perspicacity surpass a hundred generations; your subject obtains the honor of receiving the tone in person—a moment once in a thousand years."
idiomatic: "Your Majesty's sagacity surpasses a hundred generations. To receive your teaching in person is a moment that comes once in a thousand years."

literal: On the northern campaign against the Mian he was given three thousand bolts of silk.
idiomatic: On the campaign north of the Mian he was given three thousand bolts of silk.

literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of All Armies on the Southern Expedition, Grand General of the Center Army, and Opener of the Office.
idiomatic: He was made bearer of the staff, commander of all armies on the southern expedition, grand general of the center army, and opener of the office.

literal: Again an edict said: "Tomorrow we will meet the enemy; you may order the officers and soldiers to make their army bearing solemn.
idiomatic: An edict added, "Tomorrow we engage the enemy. Order the troops to dress their ranks."

literal: " Xie thereupon personally drilled the great host.
idiomatic: Xie personally drilled the great host.

literal: In a moment two great birds came from the south; one toward the traveling palace, one toward the command tent; each was caught by men.
idiomatic: Soon two great birds flew from the south—one toward the traveling palace, one toward headquarters—and each was caught.

literal: Xie said to Gaozu: "At first one bird, seeing the banners, fell headlong; your subject called it great good fortune.
idiomatic: Xie told Gaozu, "Earlier one bird fell before our banners. I called that great fortune."

literal: " Gaozu jested with him: "Birds fear authority—is it only the center army's stratagem? I too share a portion.
idiomatic: Gaozu teased him, "Birds fear majesty—is that only your stratagem? I claim a share."

literal: This is moreover great good; and all the military texts say so.
idiomatic: "This is great good fortune, and every military classic says so."

literal: " At dawn they utterly defeated Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan.
idiomatic: At dawn they shattered Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan.

literal: That night came great rain; Gaozu said: "In old times one heard that when the state's army won, clouds and rain always followed.
idiomatic: That night a great rain fell. Gaozu said, "They say that when the state's army wins, clouds and rain follow."

literal: Now having taken Xinye and Nanyang and broken this bandit, timely moisture has indeed descended.
idiomatic: "Having taken Xinye and Nanyang and broken this enemy, timely rain has come as promised."

literal: Truly this saying.
idiomatic: "The saying is true."

literal: " Xie replied: "The response of the water virtue has long been called the heart of Heaven.
idiomatic: Xie answered, "The response of water's virtue has long been called Heaven's own mind."

literal: Gaozu ordered Xie to compose a victory bulletin; Xie declined and said: "Your subject has heard that a victory bulletin is spread to the four seas and exposed to all ears; it must proclaim martial prestige to show the realm.
idiomatic: Gaozu ordered Xie to draft the victory bulletin. Xie declined: "A victory bulletin is spread to the four seas and shown to every ear. It must proclaim our martial prestige to the world."

literal: Your subject's small talent is not enough for great use.
idiomatic: "My small talent is not fit for so great a use."

literal: " Gaozu said: "You are not only close by imperial command—you are also accomplished in talent; only compose it.
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "You are not only my kin by decree—you are accomplished. Write it."

literal: " When it was done it especially resembled the emperor's own writing; those who saw it all said it was the imperial brush.
idiomatic: When it was done it read like the emperor's own hand; all who saw it took it for his writing.

literal: Gaozu said: "What you composed people say I made; if not elder brother then younger brother—who can tell?
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "People say I wrote what you wrote. Between brothers, who can tell?"

literal: " Xie replied: "Zixia was slandered before the sage; your subject again bears blame in the coming age."
idiomatic: Xie answered, "Zixia was slandered before the sage; I again bear blame for the age to come."

literal: When they reached Yuzhou Gaozu wrote a family letter to Xie saying: "Teaching the wind is minute and close; ritual and government are stern and strict—if one does not with deep heart daily urge, how can one honor them?
idiomatic: At Yuzhou Gaozu wrote Xie a family letter: "Teaching and custom are subtle; ritual and government are strict. Without daily urging from the heart, how can they be honored?"

literal: I have often wished to establish one clan master to make solemn our primal clan.
idiomatic: "I have long wished to set one master over the clan to make our house solemn."

literal: You are kin at the pole star's height and stand as Director at the Center; in bearing and talent you are truly fit to be a model.
idiomatic: "You are kin at the throne's height and stand as director at the center. In bearing and talent you are truly fit to be the model."

literal: Repeated oral commands you still held in modest refusal; hard to go against pure restraint—time has slipped until now.
idiomatic: "I have commanded you again and again, yet you still refuse in modesty. I could not override your restraint, and time has slipped by."

literal: The weight of clan regulation—on whom else can it be laid?
idiomatic: "The weight of clan law—on whom else can I lay it?"

literal: Henceforth entrust clan ritual to you; let the charge be fulfilled on your person; where teaching and canon are not followed, report each matter as it arises and I will separately make it solemn.
idiomatic: "Entrust clan ritual to you and let the charge rest on you. Where teaching is not followed, report each case and I will correct it."

literal: If among the imperial clan there is fault and it is concealed and not reported, the bell punishment falls on your person.
idiomatic: "If any in the clan offends and you conceal it, the penalty falls on you."

literal: Net and warp mutually urging—perhaps there will be urging to reform.
idiomatic: "Let the net and the warp urge one another—perhaps there will be reform."

literal: I hear in the morning and die at evening—there is no regret in that.
idiomatic: "If I hear at dawn and die at dusk, I shall not regret it."

literal: " The next day Xie spoke to his face and said: "Receiving the command to specialize in clan regulation and to investigate what violates it.
idiomatic: The next day Xie spoke plainly: "I have received command to oversee clan regulation and investigate violations."

literal: Your subject has heard: 'When the person is upright, orders proceed without being issued; when the person is not upright, though orders are issued they are not followed.'
idiomatic: "I have heard: when the person is upright, orders run without being given; when the person is crooked, orders are given yet not followed."

literal: Your subject, placed among the clan, lacks the obedience of elder and younger; in receiving others lacks the ritual of a state's scholar; each time on petition I have already received compassionate indulgence.
idiomatic: "Among the clan I lack proper deference between elder and younger; in dealing with others I lack a statesman's ritual. Each time I have petitioned you have indulged me."

literal: I did not expect that in this present command there would in the end be no sparing.
idiomatic: "I did not expect this command to spare me in the end."

literal: I still hope for sage compassion and a grant of release and completion.
idiomatic: "I still beg your compassion to release me and let the charge be complete elsewhere."

literal: " Gaozu said: "You are harmonious—go and revere it.
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "You are fit—go and honor the charge."

literal: " Xie memorialized to offer one year's state revenue, salary, and kin stipend to supplement army and state; an edict said: "Cutting the body to preserve the state—its principle is far-reaching.
idiomatic: Xie memorialized to give one year's state revenue, salary, and kin stipend to the army and state. The edict read, "To cut from oneself to preserve the realm is principle of the farthest reach."

literal: But because you are my kin, [1] you thereby reduced yourself to aid the state.
idiomatic: "Yet because you are my kin,[1] you have reduced yourself to aid the state."

literal: Salary is stopped; for kin and state affairs, hear and receive one part in three."
idiomatic: "Your salary is stopped; for kin and state obligations you may still receive one part in three."

literal: When Gaozu was unwell Xie attended within on medicine and without summed the affairs of army and state; far and near were solemn and none had a different opinion.
idiomatic: When Gaozu fell ill Xie tended him within on medicine and without held army and state together; far and near were orderly and none disputed it.

literal: Xu Jie was the foremost physician of the age; earlier he had taken leave to return to Luoyang; when summoned and arrived Xie led him to a separate place, weeping and taking his hand, and said to him: "Sir, you are the age's primal transformer; the utmost venerable's breath and strength are critically weak; I wish you to exhaust your heart and think only on prescriptions and treatment.
idiomatic: Xu Jie was the age's finest physician. He had been on leave in Luoyang; when summoned, Xie led him aside, wept, took his hand, and said, "You are the age's great healer. The emperor's strength is critically weak. Exhaust your heart on his cure alone."

literal: If the holy body daily grows healthy and thereby the four seas have reliance, you will obtain reward beyond expectation;
idiomatic: "If he recovers and the realm has someone to rely on, you will receive reward beyond measure;"

literal: if not, then there will be punishment beyond reckoning—not only glory and shame but existence and extinction hang on this.
idiomatic: "if not, punishment beyond reckoning—not only honor and shame but life and death hang on it."

literal: Sir, exert yourself!
idiomatic: "Exert yourself!"

literal: " Those at left and right who saw it all sobbed.
idiomatic: Those who witnessed it sobbed.

literal: When he was introduced Jie at once wished to advance treatment.
idiomatic: When Xu Jie was brought in he wished to treat him at once.

literal: Because Gaozu's divine strength was weak Xie only ordered food flavors for restorative care.
idiomatic: Because Gaozu's strength was feeble, Xie allowed only restorative food and gentle care.

literal: Xie then secretly made an altar on the bank of the Ru River, following the Duke of Zhou's precedent, reporting to Heaven and Earth and Xianwen to request life, begging with his own body in substitution.
idiomatic: Xie then secretly built an altar on the Ru's bank, following the Duke of Zhou's example, reporting to Heaven and Earth and Xianwen to beg for life, offering his own body in substitution.
